key_insight: Light can reversibly trigger defect-free halide swapping in 2D mixed-halide perovskites because photo-induced lattice forces and carrier–phonon coupling drive ion motion along the exchange pathway without fully crossing the ground-state barrier.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new route to reusable, self-resetting photo-switchable perovskite devices for tunable optics and optoelectronics without relying on defect-mediated degradation.
method: Nudged elastic band calculations to map the halide-exchange energy barrier
Photo-force calculations to quantify non-equilibrium light-driven work on ions
Lattice dynamics and GW optical calculations to connect phonons, band structure, and light-induced spectral shifts
evidence_signal: The model reproduces the experimentally observed absorption spectrum in the dark and predicts a clear light-induced redshift from bandgap renormalization, consistent with reversible switching.
watch_item: The effect depends on specific soft phonon modes and strong light-lattice coupling, so performance may be sensitive to material composition, excitation conditions, and stability outside the modeled regime.
paper_title: Reversible photo-switching optical functionality in two-dimensional mixed-halide hybrid perovskites
